_note: Synthetic (imaginary) virtual city for scripts/synthetic_city.py. Every number is an assumption made because no real building/GIS data may be used — none is a measurement. Change values here, not in code.

site._note: Real neighbourhood (AGENTS.md step R, user approval 2026-11-05: public data allowed) built by twin/site.py from OpenStreetMap buildings and the Copernicus GLO-30 surface model. Unlike the rest of this file these are choices about real data, not an imaginary city; the building-storey defaults are assumptions for central Seoul, not measurements.
site.name: Gangnam station area, Seoul
site.bbox_note: West, south, east, north in degrees (about 1.06 km x 1.11 km) around Gangnam station.
site.cell_m_note: Hydraulic raster cell size (m): fine enough to resolve streets about 20 m wide and building blocks, coarse enough for the explicit solver to stay fast. An assumption.
site.osm_file_note: Geofabrik South Korea extract (OSM data of 2026-10-13) in paths.osm_dir().
site.dem_file_note: Copernicus GLO-30 surface model tile (about 30 m, EPSG:4326) in paths.external_dir('copernicus_dem'); it includes buildings and trees, so footprints are masked and the ground interpolated.
site.floor_to_floor_m_note: Assumed storey height (m) used to turn building:levels or default levels into a height; typical 3.0-3.6 m for Korean offices and apartments.

default_levels._note: Assumed number of storeys by OSM building value when the footprint has neither a height nor a building:levels tag; numbers are assumptions for central Seoul, not measurements. Unlisted values fall back to 'yes'.

attribution._note: Credits required by the data licences; show them wherever the site is displayed.
attribution.osm_note: OpenStreetMap building footprints and tags, Open Database License.
attribution.dem: Copernicus DEM GLO-30, (c) DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and (c) Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018 provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA; all rights reserved
attribution.dem_note: Copernicus GLO-30 surface model, ESA / European Union licence.

heat._note: Street-canyon heat proxy (twin/heat.py; AGENTS.md step 8), repo-specific and NOT UTCI: no UTCI library is installed. Air temperature per return period, plus urban-heat-island, sky-view factor and sunlit fraction of an infinite street canyon, give a weighted feels-like temperature priced through the repo's heat-productivity curve. Every value is an assumption, not a fitted climatology.
heat.return_periods_note: Assumed heatwave return periods (years), the same ladder as the flood events.
heat.t_air_2y_c_note: Assumed 2-year peak daily-maximum air temperature (degC) for a Korean mid-latitude city; an assumption, not a station record.
heat.t_air_slope_c_note: Assumed Gumbel-like growth of the peak air temperature per ln-year (degC), so the 100-year peak is about 5.5 degC above the 2-year peak. An assumption.
heat.mrt_sun_excess_c_note: Assumed extra mean radiant temperature (degC) over air temperature for a fully sunlit street at midsummer noon; an assumption in the usual 20-30 degC range for hot sunny days.
heat.mrt_sky_excess_c_note: Assumed extra radiant load (degC) from the open sky and warm surfaces, scaled by the sky-view factor; an assumption.
heat.wind_10m_ms_note: Assumed 10 m wind speed (m/s) for the UTCI on a calm summer afternoon; UTCI is valid for 0.5-17 m/s.
heat.rh_pct_note: Assumed relative humidity (%) at the afternoon temperature peak of a Korean heatwave.
heat.mrt_weight_note: Assumed weight of the radiant excess in the feels-like temperature (a person feels air temperature plus a fraction of the radiant excess); an assumption, not a UTCI regression. Used only by feels_like (the earlier proxy); the hazard now uses UTCI.
heat.solar_elevation_deg_note: Assumed solar elevation (degrees) at midsummer noon near 37 N (90 - 37 + 23.4 = 76 at solstice, lowered for typical heatwave dates); an assumption.
heat.street_width_m_note: Assumed street width (m) between building faces, a typical Korean two-lane street with pavements; one value for the whole synthetic city.

uhi_c._note: Assumed urban-heat-island air-temperature excess (degC) per asset kind: dense paved or hot-process lots are warmer than residential ones. Assumptions, not measurements.

workers._note: Assumed workers per asset (people present in the heat) used for the productivity exposure. Roads carry no workers: they have no payroll, so their exposure is zero. Assumptions, not a census.

heat.daily_wage_usd_note: Assumed daily labour value (USD per worker-day) for a mid-income Korean city; an assumption.
heat.heatwave_days_note: Assumed number of heatwave working days per year over which the peak-day productivity loss applies; an assumption.

max_mdd._note: Assumed maximum productivity loss at the top of the repo's heat ramp, per asset kind: higher for outdoor or heavy work (industrial, roads) and lower for air-conditioned work (commercial, hospital). Assumptions, not published curves.

coast._note: Synthetic sea coast for the storm-surge scenario (twin/coastal.py; AGENTS.md step 9). In this scenario the bank (row 0 side) faces the sea: the river and coastal scenarios are alternatives on the same terrain, not both present at once. The coast is synthetic, a straight east-west line; CLIMADA's real distance-to-coast raster is not used. Every value is an assumption.
coast.coastline_offset_m_note: Assumed distance (m) of the coastline south of grid row 0. Must equal (n + 0.5) x hydraulic.cell_m so the coast falls on a raster cell edge and no DEM cell straddles it: land cells fill the gap, sea cells start beyond it.
coast.sea_rows_note: Assumed number of sea raster rows written south of the coast in the DEM (at least this many rows at sea_bed_m).
coast.sea_bed_m_note: Assumed sea-bed elevation (m, negative = below datum) of the sea rows; shallow shelf, a placeholder.
coast.inland_decay_m_per_km_note: Surge height lost per km inland (m/km); the CLIMADA Petals default from Pielke and Pielke (1997).
coast.sea_level_rise_m_note: Sea-level rise added to the surge (m); 0.0 is present day, raise it for a climate scenario.
coast.surge_duration_h_note: Assumed duration (h) of the raised-cosine surge wave at the coast in the 2D model (rise, peak at half, fall); a typhoon surge lasts hours, not days. Kept short on purpose: the city is only ~2 km deep and fills within minutes, so durations of 3 h and more all give the bathtub (differences < 0.1 m in total) and only a shorter surge shows the 2D effect. Only the 2D model uses it; the Petals bathtub assumes the water stays up long enough to fill every low cell.
coast.surge_recession_h_note: Assumed time (h) the 2D run continues after the surge wave so that water on land can settle.

typhoon._note: Synthetic typhoon tracks (twin/typhoon.py; AGENTS.md step 7). Straight, constant-intensity hourly tracks aimed at the city centre with a random lateral offset and heading; wind is CLIMADA's Holland profile; priced with the repo's TC regional impact function for Korea. Every value is an assumption, not a fitted climatology.
typhoon.n_tracks_note: Assumed number of synthetic tracks, each given the same annual frequency.
typhoon.annual_rate_per_year_note: Assumed total rate (1/yr) of typhoons passing near the city, split equally over the tracks; a placeholder of the order of Korean landfall counts, not a measurement.
typhoon.vmax_ms_note: Assumed range of maximum sustained wind (m/s), drawn uniformly per track.
typhoon.rmax_km_note: Assumed radius of maximum wind range (km), drawn uniformly per track.
typhoon.speed_kmh_note: Assumed translation speed range (km/h), drawn uniformly per track.
typhoon.heading_deg_note: Assumed heading range (deg clockwise from north): north to north-east, typical of storms recurving over Korea.
typhoon.miss_distance_km_note: Assumed maximum lateral offset (km) of a track from the city centre, drawn uniformly in [-miss, +miss].
typhoon.start_distance_km_note: Assumed distance (km) from the track start back along its heading to the city centre.
typhoon.hours_note: Assumed track length (h); long enough for the slowest storm to pass the city.

grid._note: rows x cols intersections of a street grid; row 0 is the river bank, rows increase inland.

terrain._note: ground elevation above the river datum: z = bank_m + slope_m_per_m * distance_inland + N(0, noise_sd_m), floored at 0.

flood._note: river stage above datum at return period RP: h(RP) = stage_2y_m + stage_slope_m * ln(RP / 2). One layered event per RP, frequency 1/RP_i - 1/RP_{i+1}, the rarest keeps 1/RP.

hydraulic._note: 2D local-inertial flood model (twin/hydraulics.py, twin/inundation.py; AGENTS.md step 6B). The river row follows a raised-cosine stage hydrograph from base_stage_m up to the stage-law peak h(T) and back over flood_duration_h; the run continues recession_h after it. Every number is an assumption, not a calibration.
hydraulic.cell_m_note: raster cell size (m); must divide grid.spacing_m an even number of times so road midpoints fall on a cell centre.
hydraulic.manning_n_note: Manning roughness (s m^-1/3) for an urban floodplain with buildings and streets; typical published range 0.03-0.1.
hydraulic.river_bed_m_note: bed of the river row below datum (m), so the channel holds water at the base stage.
hydraulic.base_stage_m_note: river stage before and after the flood wave (m above datum).
hydraulic.flood_duration_h_note: length of the flood wave (h); the peak is at half this time. A short (flashy) wave leaves less time to fill the city than the bathtub assumes.
hydraulic.recession_h_note: extra simulated time after the wave (h).
hydraulic.alpha_cfl_note: time-step safety factor of de Almeida et al. (2012), 0 < alpha < 1.
hydraulic.max_valid_froude_note: the local-inertial scheme drops advection; runs whose peak Froude number reaches this are flagged as outside validity (Neal et al. 2012; tests/test_hydraulics.py).

loss._note: Per-building loss of one design storm on the real site (twin/site_loss.py; AGENTS.md step R3). Building values are NOT client data: footprint area (OSM) x exposed storeys x an assumed replacement cost per m2. Every number here is an assumption; the loss is the loss of ONE storm, not an expected annual loss.
loss.entry_threshold_m_note: No-damage threshold T (m), method of the user's sheet 무피해문턱_계산표(261020): damage 0 while outside depth <= T, the unchanged JRC Asia curve at the full depth once over T (FLOPROS-style rule, Scussolini et al. 2016). 0.05 m is the sheet's default when no survey value exists: the JRC curve as implemented in CLIMADA-petals is already 0 at 0.05 m, so nothing extra is blocked. No Korean standard value for entrance sills was found (sheet source F1), so no larger sill is assumed. Per-building sills, flood barriers, ground-floor heights and pumps (sheet steps 1-5) need survey data and are not available for OSM buildings.
loss.max_exposed_storeys_note: assumption: street water reaches the ground floor only, so the JRC curve applies to one storey of floor area; upper floors of tall buildings are not exposed. Basement car parks are NOT modelled (a known gap: most 2022 Gangnam damage was in basements).

cost_usd_per_m2._note: assumption: replacement cost per m2 of floor (USD), of the order of Korean reinforced-concrete new-build unit costs (about 2.0-2.5 million KRW/m2 at about 1,350 KRW/USD); not a citation of a published table, contents not included.

property_type._note: OSM building value -> engine property_type (physical_risk_config.json maps it to the JRC sector); unlisted values use _default.

loss.underground_property_type_note: Underground features (Gangnam Station Underground Shopping Center) are shops: one storey, commercial curve, filled by the street water above the threshold over their footprint (capped at one storey).

basement._note: Basement storeys of above-ground buildings on the real site (twin/basement.py; AGENTS.md step R3c), following the user's sheets 층별_침수피해율_비교(261020) (storey-weighted value, default basement storeys by use) and 지하침수_시험계산 (ramp entrance as a broad-crested weir). OSM has no basement data: every number here is an assumption or a sheet default, not a survey value. Street water entering a basement is NOT removed from the 2D street flow (one-way coupling).

levels._note: Default basement storeys by OSM building value, from the storey sheet's defaults when the location is unknown (office 4, retail/hotel 3, residential 2, logistics 1); unlisted values use _default. school, church, public, university (1) and hospital (2) are reviewer assumptions added in R3d: the sheet covers commercial assets only.

basement.min_storeys_note: assumption: only buildings with at least this many above-ground storeys get basements; small low-rise buildings in OSM are not assumed to have basement car parks.
basement.ramp_width_m_note: Sheet default (무피해문턱_계산표 L1): two-lane ramp, 주차장법 시행규칙 제6조제1항제5호 (6 m or more); one ramp per building assumed.
basement.weir_coefficient_note: Broad-crested weir, Q = C B H^1.5 with C = (2/3)^1.5 sqrt(g) = 1.705 m^0.5/s (Henderson 1966, sheet H1); theoretical, an upper bound on inflow.
basement.ramp_rain_area_m2_note: Sheet assumption (지하침수_시험계산): ramp (6 m x about 30 m) plus a dry area of about 20 m2; all rain on it (runoff coefficient 1) goes down.
basement.pump_m3_h_note: Drainage pumps are survey data, not available for OSM buildings: 0 (conservative, like the sheet's sump capacity 0).

rain._note: Design-storm rain on the real site (twin/pluvial.py; AGENTS.md step R2). Repo-specific pluvial method (design storm, NRCS CN, uniform sewer sink); every number is an assumption, not a calibration or a reconstruction of an observed event.
rain.total_mm_note: assumption: storm depth (mm) over duration_min, of the order of the 8 Aug 2022 Seoul downpour (more than 100 mm/h at its peak); NOT a reconstruction of observations.
rain.duration_min_note: assumption: a two-hour storm; the hyetograph is stretched over this time.
rain.cumulative_fraction_note: assumed shape: cumulative rain as a fraction of the total at 0, 10, ..., 100 % of the storm; intensity peaks in the 4th to 6th tenth like a Huff 2nd/3rd-quartile storm. To be replaced by the MOLIT Huff coefficients for Seoul.
rain.recession_min_note: assumption: extra simulated time after the storm (min) so water can drain and pond.
rain.cn_paved_note: NRCS (SCS) curve number of an impervious urban surface, TR-55 (USDA 1986); applied to every cell, roofs and streets alike.
rain.sewer_capacity_mm_h_note: assumption: Seoul's former 30-year design standard for storm sewers (mm/h), taken as a uniform drain on every open cell; real capacity varies by pipe and is not modelled.
rain.edge_slope_note: assumption: bed slope (-) for Manning normal-flow outflow through the site edges.

climate._note: Climate-change river stage shift vs the present baseline. The future stage law is h_future(T) = (stage_2y_m + stage_2y_m_shift) + (stage_slope_m + stage_slope_m_shift)*ln(T/2); return periods and centroid positions are unchanged, so the future hazard is compared event-for-event with the present. Defence design depths are derived from the PRESENT hazard and applied fixed to the future hazard — defences keep their present height and do not grow with the flood (see compare_climate in twin/pipeline.py and AGENTS.md step 3). A scenario with shift 0 is equivalent to the present.

future_scenarios._note: Mid-century-style +0.5 m uniform stage rise on the 2-year stage; stage growth slope unchanged. This is the scenario the climate-change multiplier table is built against (AGENTS.md: the +0.5 m trap case).
future_scenarios.name: +0.5m

levee._note: A LOCAL levee on part of the bank: a 100-year levee along the river reach of cols 5..14 protects the floodplain behind it (all rows of those cols); the other cols stay undefended. Flanking (water going round the levee ends) is ignored until the step-6 hydraulic model. Applied per centroid with protection.protect: depths from events up to the design return period are removed, rarer overtopping events flood at full depth. rows/cols are inclusive grid-index bands, same convention as zoning.

zoning._note: row/col bands (inclusive) that decide each intersection's land use; everything else is residential.

facilities._note: special nodes as [row, col]. Substations and the hospital are the targets of the network-failure test.

values_usd._note: replacement value per lot (median), lognormal spread sigma; roads are priced per metre of segment.

property_type._note: property_type handed to the engine; physical_risk_config.json maps it to the JRC sector.

network._note: a node (intersection, substation, hospital) is out of service when its flood depth exceeds failure_depth_m — an assumed passability/operability limit, not a damage curve.

buildings._note: Synthetic 3D building geometry for the deck.gl city_3d.html viewer (AGENTS.md step 5). Footprint size and storey count are drawn per zone with the spec seed and are GEOMETRY ONLY in this step: they do not touch the pricing/damage model, so NO EAL number changes. The storey count is intended to drive the ground-floor / basement EXPOSURE in a later step; wiring storeys into the engine calculate is deliberately deferred (see AGENTS.md 'storeys feed the ground-floor/basement exposure'). Footprints are drawn smaller than spacing_m/2 so lots on adjacent intersections never overlap. Building height = storeys * floor_to_floor_m.
buildings.floor_to_floor_m_note: Assumed storey-to-storey height (m): typical floor-to-floor (structural zone + services slab). Same constant for every zone; only the storey count varies by land use.

per_kind._note: Footprint ([x, y] metres) and storey-count ([min, max]) ranges drawn per lot with the spec seed. Every value is an assumption, not a measurement.

residential.footprint_m_note: Small low-rise lots: footprint kept well under half the 100 m spacing so detached/semi-detached blocks do not touch their neighbours.
residential.storeys_note: One to three storeys: single-family homes and small apartment blocks on the residential grid.

commercial.footprint_m_note: Larger footprints on the commercial street front (commercial_rows x commercial_cols): bigger low- to mid-rise blocks.
commercial.storeys_note: Three to eight storeys: low- and mid-rise office/retail blocks on the commercial front.

industrial.footprint_m_note: Wide single- to low-rise plant footprints along the river industrial rows.
industrial.storeys_note: One to three storeys: warehouses and light industry; predominantly single-storey plant.

substation.footprint_m_note: Compact fenced infrastructure footprint for the assumed substation lots.
substation.storeys_note: One to two storeys: ground-level plant plus a small control/measuring room.

hospital.footprint_m_note: Large footprint for the single city-general hospital lot.
hospital.storeys_note: Four to eight storeys: a multi-storey clinical block as the city's tallest facility.

rain_frequency._note: Step R3b: return-period ladder of 2-hour storms from the KMA ASOS Seoul (108) hourly record (기상청_지상(종관, ASOS) 시간자료 조회서비스, data.go.kr 15057210, 1961-), files in paths.kma_dir()/asos_hourly/<station>. Annual maxima of the window_h-hour total, L-moment fit (Hosking 1990; GEV by Hosking, Wallis & Wood 1985), bootstrap band. One station 7 km from the site; local storms can differ (validated against the Seoul flood-trace maps in a later step).
rain_frequency.window_h_note: matches rain.duration_min (120 min): the ladder storm keeps the hyetograph shape and only its total changes.
rain_frequency.distribution_note: GEV by L-moments; the Gumbel fit is reported alongside (MOLIT 확률강우량도 practice uses Gumbel).

validation._note: Step R4: building-level check of the twin against the Seoul flood-trace maps (서울시 침수흔적도, 서울 열린데이터광장 OA-15636, 공공누리 제1유형; paths.external_dir('seoul_flood_traces')/<year>). Polygons are only queried (footprint + buffer intersects a trace), never rasterised or shipped. 2022 is run with the observed 10-min rain of the nearest Seoul rain gauges (서울시 강우량 정보 OA-1168, 공공누리 제2유형: internal calibration only, never shipped; paths.external_dir('seoul_rain_gauges')). 2010 and 2011 have no gauge files, so they are checked for spatial pattern only (design-storm shape, total chosen so the modelled flooded street area matches the traced area).
validation.buffer_m_note: assumption: traces are digitised at street scale and the DEM is 30 m; a building counts as observed-flooded when a trace lies within this distance of its footprint.

2022.name: 2022-08-08 집중호우
2022.gauges_note: 서초구청 1.5 km, 강남구청 2.9 km, 반포펌프장 3.0 km from the site centre
